prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares after coordination; Business Rules Registry supplies thresholds): Normal Operations; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor extend metering horizon; RFM may combine arrival regulation+departure metering); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance State; Winter(MBO confirms in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity). Actors: Regional Flow Manager(RFM; staged rate increase only after Ironleaf confirms stable spacing), Airspace Sector Planner(Sector Load Monitor), Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor(North/South Runway Meter; Quartzline pad releases), ADM(records surface-constraint significance in Foxglove), Ramp Control Lead(verifies unavailable bridge/GPU/hydrant/taxilane scope: single movement, stand group, apron route), Aircraft Operator Representative, Airline Operations Coordinator(decides keep TOBT/new TOBT/later CTT), Slot Coordinator(reviews CTT vs surface release time for regulated flights before accepting metering), Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher(Handling Resource Planner), Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO. Halcyon logs push rationale. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(correlates surface equipment with flight intent, stand, runway plan before recommending changes; surface constraints=tactical capacity inputs). Parts: Integrated Tactical Management Position; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(Flight Intent Message stream; regulation when demand>Airport Acceptance Rate); CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(converts persistent surface constraints into reduced stand throughput/turn buffers/taxi-out); Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal; Emberline=Departure Metering Service(runway metering limits→candidate pushback spacing→Blueharbor; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Ironleaf uses fuel hold advice to avoid sequencing ahead of active fueling constraint; North Runway Meter(cuts release rate as runway-entry queues near threshold); South Runway Meter(same, separated from arrival regulation); Surface Surveillance Adapter(occupancy+equipment status→Ramp Movement Board, Ironleaf); Ramp Movement Board(apron congestion advisories on conflicting pushbacks, blocked lead-ins, saturated holding points, wingtip clearance); Airline Interface Adapter(produces Late

New part:
S459: The Gate Conflict Detector checks whether the congestion can be relieved by resequencing adjacent stands before the system proposes a broader departure delay.
S460: The Handling Resource Planner evaluates whether additional ground handling resources can remove the constraint faster than a flow management measure would absorb it.
S461: Lantern must distribute surface equipment and apron congestion advisories to subscribed operational roles within the latency target defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S462: The Common Situation Display highlights active surface advisories with the affected stands, taxi segments, runway meters, and flight identifiers visible to authorized users.
S463: The Regional Flow Manager uses these advisories to decide whether the tactical plan should retain normal sequencing, shift to local metering, or support a Tactical Regulation Proposal.
S464: During Adverse Weather Mode, the same surface advisories carry higher planning weight because reduced visibility and wet pavement increase the cost of taxiway conflicts and blocked stands.
S465: During the Recovery Phase, the system prioritizes removal of surface holds that constrain multiple rotations before optimizing isolated punctuality impacts.
S466: Every accepted surface equipment, fuel hold, runway metering, or apron congestion adjustment is written to the Collaborative Decision Log and the Audit Event Ledger with the actor, timestamp, affected flight, and planning rationale.
S467: Stand, gate, and passenger connection recovery begins after surface constraints have been reduced enough for individual aircraft rotations to become the controlling problem.
S468: The Gate Conflict Detector compares planned arrivals, planned departures, assigned gates, towing availability, and published stand status to identify conflicts that would otherwise be hidden inside local spreadsheets.
S469: The Ramp Movement Board maintains the operational view of occupied, blocked, cleaning, boarding, and tow-ready positions so that ramp decisions are based on the same stand timeline used by airport and airline users.
S470: The Airport CDM Portal presents each gate conflict with the affected flights, passenger connection exposure, aircraft size compatibility, and the latest feasible off-block time.
S471: The Airport Duty Manager sets the recovery priority for stands that can be reopened quickly, giving preference to positions that remove multiple downstream conflicts rather than a single isolated delay.
S472: Airline Operations Coordinator uses the Gate Reopening Memo to confirm when a previously unavailable gate can be planned again for arrival handling, boarding, and connection recovery.
S473: The Ramp Control Lead coordinates stand reopening with the Ground Handling Dispatcher so that ground equipment, marshalling staff, and safe access routes are available before a flight is reassigned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
